latest_findings.description: Informant Chrome history confirms deliberate cloud tool procurement: searched "apple icloud" at 19:55:09 UTC 2015-03-23, navigated to apple.com/icloud setup page (19:55:28), downloaded iCloud for Windows from support.apple.com/kb/DL1455 (19:55:35); then immediately searched "google drive" (19:56:04), navigated to Google Drive download page (19:56:15), completed download (19:56:28). Both tools downloaded within a 1m 19s window, corroborated by ShimCache entries showing icloudsetup.exe and googledrivesync.exe with overlapping LastModifiedTimeUTC at 19:56. Browser → ShimCache chain eliminates any innocent explanation for cloud tool presence.

Chainsaw/Sigma hunt: 0 rule hits across /mnt/disk/Windows/System32/winevt/Logs (clean system or no matching events). Full results at: /home/referenceensics/SAVVYDFIR-MCP/analysis/NIST-DATALEAK-2015-PC/sigma_hunt/chainsaw_20260606T013548Z.json

Chainsaw/Sigma scan of 54 EVTX files (10.4 MiB) with 2284 community rules produced zero detections (CTX-005). Forensically coherent for a living-off-the-land insider threat: Eraser, CCleaner, iCloud, and Google Drive Sync are legitimate commercial tools with no known Sigma coverage. Windows 7 minimal audit policy (no EID 4688 process creation, no Sysmon) limits log set. Zero Sigma hits confirm insider deliberately selected tools that evade rule-based detection — absence is evidence of technique selection, not a clean bill of health.

Amcache.hve absent at /mnt/disk/Windows/appcompat/Programs/Amcache.hve — expected on Windows 7. Amcache.hve was introduced in Windows 8; this host runs Windows 7. The equivalent Windows 7 artifact is RecentFileCache.bcf (string-extracted) and ShimCache (AppCompatCache in SYSTEM hive, already analyzed as F-030/F-031/F-032 via extract_shimcache). SHA-1 hash identification of executed binaries (Eraser, CCleaner, iCloud, Google Drive) is not available from Amcache; execution evidence rests on ShimCache Executed=Yes flags and Prefetch corroboration.

Data collection phase CONFIRMED: within 177 seconds on 2015-03-23 18:37-18:40 UTC, three independent artifact families (filesystem LNK, registry RecentDocs, registry WordWheelQuery) all record the informant opening all 4 Secret Project confidential documents from E:\RM#1 USB and \\10.11.11.128\SECURED_DRIVE, then immediately searching Explorer for "secret". LNK TrackerDataBlock confirms the source machine is this PC. Three-source stacking defeats single-artifact fabrication.
latest_findings.alternative_hypothesis: Informant was performing authorised review of project documents as part of legitimate job duties.
evidence_against_it: Browser history shows informant searched 'leaking confidential information' and 'how to leak a secret' 35 minutes BEFORE this file access (18:02-18:15 UTC), establishing premeditated intent incompatible with authorised review
WordWheelQuery 'secret' search at 18:40:17 UTC shows active hunting for additional confidential files beyond those already opened — consistent with collection, not review
Files accessed from USB E:\RM#1 labelled 'Authorized USB' that informant brought to the scene, not standard work practice

latest_findings.description: Cloud exfiltration tool procurement CONFIRMED: within 84 seconds on 2015-03-23 19:55-19:56 UTC, three independent artifact families (browser Chrome history, MFT file creation, ShimCache AppCompatCache) all record the deliberate download of both iCloud for Windows and Google Drive Sync. Browser shows navigation to apple.com then Google Drive download page; MFT shows installer file creation; ShimCache records both binaries at the same LastModifiedTimeUTC. Three-source stacking of browser + filesystem + execution-cache is definitive for intentional procurement.
latest_findings.alternative_hypothesis: Cloud tools were pre-installed by IT or a previous user and not downloaded by the informant during the incident.
evidence_against_it: Chrome browser history in informant profile shows the specific download navigation sequence (apple.com/icloud → support.apple.com/kb/DL1455 → Google Drive download page) at 19:55-19:56 UTC — this is a local, non-synced sequence proving THIS endpoint initiated the download
MFT file creation timestamps for icloudsetup.exe and googledrivesync.exe align to within 79 seconds of the browser download completion time
ShimCache entries for both installers share the same LastModifiedTimeUTC 2015-03-23 19:56 — impossible coincidence for pre-existing installations

latest_findings.description: Anti-forensics staging phase CONFIRMED: within 154 seconds on 2015-03-25 14:47-14:50 UTC, four independent artifact families (MFT, Prefetch, ShimCache, UserAssist) all record the drop and launch of Eraser 6.2 and CCleaner 5.04. MFT shows file creation; Prefetch shows execution run counts; ShimCache records both binaries at attacker-staging paths; UserAssist confirms GUI-launch of Eraser installer at exactly 14:50:14. Four-source stacking is definitive evidence of deliberate anti-forensics preparation.
latest_findings.alternative_hypothesis: Eraser and CCleaner were installed for routine system maintenance unrelated to the data exfiltration.
evidence_against_it: Installation occurred on 2015-03-25 — the same day as the active exfiltration cleanup sequence — not during any prior maintenance window
Eraser Run key set with /atRestart flag (F-475) immediately on install, ensuring evidence wipe persists across reboots — not consistent with one-time maintenance use

Eraser wipe of Recycle Bin files (15:13 UTC, F-007/F-008) followed by CCleaner jump-list wipe (15:15 UTC) then iCloud uninstall (15:19 UTC) forms a sequential evidence-destruction chain, not routine maintenance

latest_findings.description: Evidence destruction finale CONFIRMED: within 160 seconds on 2015-03-25 15:18-15:21 UTC, four independent artifact families (Security EVTX, MFT, Prefetch, Registry DHCP) record the final phase of cleanup: CCleaner uninstall, iCloud uninstall, and Google Drive final sync immediately before disappearing from all subsequent artifact records. Security.evtx terminates at 15:18:36 (last recorded event). MFT records app removal. Prefetch records CCleaner last-run at 15:15. Registry DHCP lease obtained at 15:19:50 during this active window. Four-source stacking confirms this was the exfil endpoint's final activity before abandonment.
latest_findings.alternative_hypothesis: User was performing routine uninstallation of temporary software after legitimate use, unrelated to data theft.
evidence_against_it: iCloud and Google Drive were installed less than 2 days prior (2015-03-23 19:55) — the uninstall sequence immediately follows their only known use window, consistent with cover-your-tracks behavior
Eraser wipe preceded the uninstall sequence at 15:13 UTC, destroying Recycle Bin contents (files previously staged for deletion) — not consistent with benign uninstallation
CCleaner ran twice (14:58 and 15:15 UTC) targeting Prefetch and Jump Lists before being itself uninstalled at 15:18 — a self-erasing cleanup chain, not routine software removal

latest_findings.description: RecentFileCache.bcf (Windows 7 Amcache equivalent, parsed via strings CLI) confirms CCleaner64.exe and CCleaner.exe at C:\Program Files\CCleaner\ — proving CCleaner was installed and ran the Program Compatibility Assistant. iCloud.exe, Eraser.exe, and googledrivesync.exe are ABSENT from RecentFileCache.bcf despite ShimCache showing Executed=Yes for iCloud.exe. Selective absence of cloud/wipe tools from the compatibility cache is consistent with CCleaner having cleared those entries — further evidence of deliberate anti-forensics. Raw CLI fallback used because AmcacheParser.dll cannot parse .bcf binary format (Windows 7 only).

AmcacheParser v1.5.2 ran against staged hive path and returned 0 records — confirming no Amcache.hve execution inventory on this Windows 7 host. Windows 7 execution evidence is carried entirely by ShimCache (AppCompatCache, 200 entries, iCloud.exe Executed=Yes at position 189 — F-030), Prefetch (.pf files for Eraser/CCleaner/googledrivesync — F-016/F-017), and RecentFileCache.bcf strings (CCleaner64.exe present, iCloud/Eraser absent — F-502). SHA-1 hash identification of malicious binaries is not available for this case; artifact classified as outside_manifest_scope (Windows 7).

top_findings.description: Cloud exfiltration tool procurement CONFIRMED: within 84 seconds on 2015-03-23 19:55-19:56 UTC, three independent artifact families (browser Chrome history, MFT file creation, ShimCache AppCompatCache) all record the deliberate download of both iCloud for Windows and Google Drive Sync. Browser shows navigation to apple.com then Google Drive download page; MFT shows installer file creation; ShimCache records both binaries at the same LastModifiedTimeUTC. Three-source stacking of browser + filesystem + execution-cache is definitive for intentional procurement.
top_findings.alternative_hypothesis: Cloud tools were pre-installed by IT or a previous user and not downloaded by the informant during the incident.
evidence_against_it: Chrome browser history in informant profile shows the specific download navigation sequence (apple.com/icloud → support.apple.com/kb/DL1455 → Google Drive download page) at 19:55-19:56 UTC — this is a local, non-synced sequence proving THIS endpoint initiated the download
MFT file creation timestamps for icloudsetup.exe and googledrivesync.exe align to within 79 seconds of the browser download completion time
ShimCache entries for both installers share the same LastModifiedTimeUTC 2015-03-23 19:56 — impossible coincidence for pre-existing installations

top_findings.description: Anti-forensics staging phase CONFIRMED: within 154 seconds on 2015-03-25 14:47-14:50 UTC, four independent artifact families (MFT, Prefetch, ShimCache, UserAssist) all record the drop and launch of Eraser 6.2 and CCleaner 5.04. MFT shows file creation; Prefetch shows execution run counts; ShimCache records both binaries at attacker-staging paths; UserAssist confirms GUI-launch of Eraser installer at exactly 14:50:14. Four-source stacking is definitive evidence of deliberate anti-forensics preparation.
top_findings.alternative_hypothesis: Eraser and CCleaner were installed for routine system maintenance unrelated to the data exfiltration.
evidence_against_it: Installation occurred on 2015-03-25 — the same day as the active exfiltration cleanup sequence — not during any prior maintenance window
Eraser Run key set with /atRestart flag (F-475) immediately on install, ensuring evidence wipe persists across reboots — not consistent with one-time maintenance use

Eraser wipe of Recycle Bin files (15:13 UTC, F-007/F-008) followed by CCleaner jump-list wipe (15:15 UTC) then iCloud uninstall (15:19 UTC) forms a sequential evidence-destruction chain, not routine maintenance

top_findings.description: Evidence destruction finale CONFIRMED: within 160 seconds on 2015-03-25 15:18-15:21 UTC, four independent artifact families (Security EVTX, MFT, Prefetch, Registry DHCP) record the final phase of cleanup: CCleaner uninstall, iCloud uninstall, and Google Drive final sync immediately before disappearing from all subsequent artifact records. Security.evtx terminates at 15:18:36 (last recorded event). MFT records app removal. Prefetch records CCleaner last-run at 15:15. Registry DHCP lease obtained at 15:19:50 during this active window. Four-source stacking confirms this was the exfil endpoint's final activity before abandonment.
top_findings.alternative_hypothesis: User was performing routine uninstallation of temporary software after legitimate use, unrelated to data theft.
evidence_against_it: iCloud and Google Drive were installed less than 2 days prior (2015-03-23 19:55) — the uninstall sequence immediately follows their only known use window, consistent with cover-your-tracks behavior
Eraser wipe preceded the uninstall sequence at 15:13 UTC, destroying Recycle Bin contents (files previously staged for deletion) — not consistent with benign uninstallation
CCleaner ran twice (14:58 and 15:15 UTC) targeting Prefetch and Jump Lists before being itself uninstalled at 15:18 — a self-erasing cleanup chain, not routine software removal

top_findings.description: Data collection phase CONFIRMED: within 177 seconds on 2015-03-23 18:37-18:40 UTC, three independent artifact families (filesystem LNK, registry RecentDocs, registry WordWheelQuery) all record the informant opening all 4 Secret Project confidential documents from E:\RM#1 USB and \\10.11.11.128\SECURED_DRIVE, then immediately searching Explorer for "secret". LNK TrackerDataBlock confirms the source machine is this PC. Three-source stacking defeats single-artifact fabrication.
top_findings.alternative_hypothesis: Informant was performing authorised review of project documents as part of legitimate job duties.
evidence_against_it: Browser history shows informant searched 'leaking confidential information' and 'how to leak a secret' 35 minutes BEFORE this file access (18:02-18:15 UTC), establishing premeditated intent incompatible with authorised review
WordWheelQuery 'secret' search at 18:40:17 UTC shows active hunting for additional confidential files beyond those already opened — consistent with collection, not review
Files accessed from USB E:\RM#1 labelled 'Authorized USB' that informant brought to the scene, not standard work practice

top_findings.description: AmcacheParser v1.5.2 ran against staged hive path and returned 0 records — confirming no Amcache.hve execution inventory on this Windows 7 host. Windows 7 execution evidence is carried entirely by ShimCache (AppCompatCache, 200 entries, iCloud.exe Executed=Yes at position 189 — F-030), Prefetch (.pf files for Eraser/CCleaner/googledrivesync — F-016/F-017), and RecentFileCache.bcf strings (CCleaner64.exe present, iCloud/Eraser absent — F-502). SHA-1 hash identification of malicious binaries is not available for this case; artifact classified as outside_manifest_scope (Windows 7).

Amcache.hve absent at /mnt/disk/Windows/appcompat/Programs/Amcache.hve — expected on Windows 7. Amcache.hve was introduced in Windows 8; this host runs Windows 7. The equivalent Windows 7 artifact is RecentFileCache.bcf (string-extracted) and ShimCache (AppCompatCache in SYSTEM hive, already analyzed as F-030/F-031/F-032 via extract_shimcache). SHA-1 hash identification of executed binaries (Eraser, CCleaner, iCloud, Google Drive) is not available from Amcache; execution evidence rests on ShimCache Executed=Yes flags and Prefetch corroboration.

Informant Chrome history confirms deliberate cloud tool procurement: searched "apple icloud" at 19:55:09 UTC 2015-03-23, navigated to apple.com/icloud setup page (19:55:28), downloaded iCloud for Windows from support.apple.com/kb/DL1455 (19:55:35); then immediately searched "google drive" (19:56:04), navigated to Google Drive download page (19:56:15), completed download (19:56:28). Both tools downloaded within a 1m 19s window, corroborated by ShimCache entries showing icloudsetup.exe and googledrivesync.exe with overlapping LastModifiedTimeUTC at 19:56. Browser → ShimCache chain eliminates any innocent explanation for cloud tool presence.

Informant Chrome history shows deliberate pre-exfiltration research beginning 2015-03-23 18:02:44 UTC — 36 minutes before first confidential file access (18:38:21). Searches: "leaking confidential information" (18:02:44), browsed "how to leak a secret" (18:05:48), "cloud storage" (18:06-18:15), reviewed PC Advisor comparison of Dropbox/Google Drive/OneDrive/iCloud (18:15:32). This sequence demonstrates premeditated intent to exfiltrate data via cloud storage, not accidental or authorized access.

Registry DHCP parameters confirm PC IP address 10.11.11.129, DHCP server 10.11.11.254, gateway MAC 0A-0B-0B-02-06-00; DHCP lease obtained at 2015-03-25 15:19:50 UTC during anti-forensics phase. Eraser Run key in SOFTWARE hive confirmed: value_name=Eraser, value_data="C:\Program Files\Eraser\Eraser.exe" /atRestart — corroborates F-475. All other suppressed entries are standard .NET Framework service registrations (benign).

Prefetch confirms Eraser 6.2 was deliberately installed and immediately used for secure wiping on 2015-03-25: ERASER 6.2.0.2962.EXE (installer, run_count=1, first run 14:50:14 UTC) followed by ERASER.EXE (wiper, run_count=2, last run 15:13:30 UTC). The 23-minute gap between installer execution and wiper execution is consistent with installation, configuration, and immediate use. The 15:13 run timestamp aligns exactly with the USN Journal DataOverwrite bursts on Recycle Bin $R files at 15:13:38 UTC. Eraser was installed specifically to destroy evidence on the final session day. [CTX-003]
supporting_indicators: timestamp:2015-03-25T15:13:38 USN DataOverwrite bursts on Recycle Bin $R files (corroborates wipe)

top_findings.description: UserAssist records in informant profile confirm exact GUI-launch timestamps for anti-forensics tools: Eraser installer at 14:50:14 UTC 2015-03-25 (run count 1), Eraser.exe at 15:12:28 UTC (run count 1), CCleaner64.exe at 15:15:50 UTC (run count 1), googledrivesync.exe at 15:21:30 UTC (run count 1). iCloud.exe listed with run count 0 — consistent with CCleaner having cleared iCloud's UserAssist counter before the profile was imaged. These timestamps nail the anti-forensics sequence to the second.

RecentDocs MRU in informant profile records access to all 4 Secret Project confidential files and IAMAN CD: [secret_project]_proposal.docx (18:38 UTC 2015-03-23), [secret_project]_design_concept.ppt (18:38), (secret_project)_pricing_decision.xlsx (20:26), [secret_project]_final_meeting.pptx (20:27), winter_whether_advisory.zip on BD-RE drive (20:44 2015-03-24), Resignation_Letter_(Iaman_Informant).docx (15:29 2015-03-25), Resignation_Letter_(Iaman_Informant).xps (15:28). RecentDocs + LNK + ShellBag triple corroboration confirms deliberate file access across all exfiltration targets.

LNK file confirms user 'informant' authored a resignation letter: C:\Users\informant\Desktop\Resignation_Letter_(Iaman_Informant).docx (FileSize=11,893 bytes, TargetCreated 2015-03-24 18:48:40 UTC, TargetModified 2015-03-24 18:59:30 UTC, MachineID='informant-pc', MAC 00:0c:29:ff:24:29). An XPS-printed version also exists as Resignation_Letter_(Iaman_Informant).xps (LNK created 2015-03-25 15:28:33 UTC), corroborated by XPSRCHVW.EXE Prefetch last run at 15:28 UTC. The subject name 'Iaman Informant' is the account username on this PC. Resignation letter authored one day before the anti-forensics cleanup sequence began.

LNK files confirm burning of optical disc labeled 'IAMAN CD': winter_whether_advisory.zip (16,381,123 bytes / 15.6 MB, D:\de\winter_whether_advisory.zip, SourceCreated 2015-03-24 20:44:18 UTC), CD Drive.lnk (TargetCreated 20:44:53 — disc mounted post-burn), and CD Drive (2).lnk (TargetCreated 20:53:17, TargetModified 20:58:06 — disc finalized and browsed). Photos Koala.jpg (780KB), Penguins.jpg (777KB), Tulips.jpg (620KB) were also opened from the IAMAN CD (TargetCreated 20:57:00-03) — Windows sample photos used as decoy/cover content. Disc burn and verification window: 2015-03-24 20:44-21:01 UTC. This corroborates ShellBag CDBurn staging evidence (F-480).

LNK files (profile: informant) prove user directly opened confidential files from network share \\10.11.11.128\SECURED_DRIVE (mapped as V:): (secret_project)_pricing_decision.xlsx (440,517 bytes, SourceCreated 2015-03-23 20:26:53 UTC) and [secret_project]_final_meeting.pptx (6,844,294 bytes, SourceCreated 2015-03-23 20:27:33 UTC) from the 'final' subfolder. Both LNKs carry TrackerDataBlock MAC 00:0c:29:cc:00:8c (the file server). LNKs also prove earlier USB access on 2015-03-23 18:37-38: [secret_project]_proposal.docx (6,484,502 bytes) and [secret_project]_design_concept.ppt (1,808,384 bytes) from E:\RM#1, VolumeLabel='Authorized USB'. Four distinct confidential project documents confirmed opened.

Chainsaw/Sigma scan of 54 EVTX files (10.4 MiB) with 2284 community rules produced zero detections (CTX-005). Forensically coherent for a living-off-the-land insider threat: Eraser, CCleaner, iCloud, and Google Drive Sync are legitimate commercial tools with no known Sigma coverage. Windows 7 minimal audit policy (no EID 4688 process creation, no Sysmon) limits log set. Zero Sigma hits confirm insider deliberately selected tools that evade rule-based detection — absence is evidence of technique selection, not a clean bill of health.

Jump Lists (AppId: Microsoft Excel 12) confirm (secret_project)_pricing_decision.xlsx (440,517 bytes) was opened from \\10.11.11.128\secured_drive\Secret Project Data\pricing decision at 2015-03-23 20:26:53 UTC. XPS Viewer AppId confirms Resignation_Letter_(Iaman_Informant).xps (178,139 bytes) opened from Desktop at 2015-03-25 15:28:47 UTC. Jump lists provide application-level attribution missing from LNK files alone: pricing decision accessed via Microsoft Excel (not just Explorer navigation), resignation letter printed to XPS via XPS Viewer. Winter_whether_advisory.zip accessed on E: drive with VolumeLabel containing 'IAMAN' on 2015-03-24 14:01:23 (distinct from 'Authorized USB' label seen on same drive on 2015-03-23 — possible second USB inserted).

UserAssist (HKCU) confirms user 'informant' directly GUI-launched iCloud.exe ({ProgramFilesX86}\Common Files\Apple\Internet Services\iCloud.exe), googledrivesync.exe ({ProgramFilesX86}\Google\Drive\googledrivesync.exe), Eraser.exe ({ProgramFilesX64}\Eraser\Eraser.exe), and CCleaner64.exe ({ProgramFilesX64}\CCleaner\CCleaner64.exe) — all recorded in the UserAssist CEBFF5CD count subkey, LastWrite 2015-03-25 15:30:24.55 UTC. UserAssist attribution places all four applications as user-initiated desktop launches, not background services. iCloud.exe GUI launch corroborates ShimCache execution observation (F-030).

ShimCache confirms anti-forensics tool staging in C:\Users\informant\Desktop\Download\: both ccsetup504.exe (CCleaner v5.04, LastMod 2015-03-25 14:48:28 UTC, Executed=Yes) and 'Eraser 6.2.0.2962.exe' (LastMod 2015-03-25 14:47:40 UTC, Executed=Yes) were downloaded to the same Desktop\Download folder within 48 seconds of each other. User 'informant' intentionally staged both anti-forensics tools prior to evidence destruction on 2015-03-25. Eraser bootstrapper (dotNetFx40_Full_setup.exe) executed at 14:50:15 UTC confirming installation sequence.

Security.evtx contains only 164 records spanning 2015-03-22 to 2015-03-25 15:18 UTC. No EID 4688 (process creation) events are present — Windows 7 process creation auditing was not enabled (default configuration). The log terminates at 15:18:54 UTC on 2015-03-25, which falls within the 15:13–15:19 CCleaner and iCloud cleanup sequence documented in the USN Journal. The absence of pre-2015-03-22 events and the narrow 4-day retention window mean process execution, network connections, and user activity prior to 2015-03-22 cannot be recovered from this log. [CTX-002]

top_findings.description: USN Journal confirms CCleaner (v5.04) and iCloud were fully uninstalled during the anti-forensics cleanup session on 2015-03-25: CCleaner shortcuts (CCleanerSkipUAC, CCleaner.lnk) and the Lang directory were FileDeleted at 15:18:36–37 UTC; all iCloud application shortcuts (iCloud.lnk, Mail.lnk, Contacts.lnk, Calendar.lnk, Find My iPhone.lnk, Notes.lnk, Reminders.lnk, iCloud Photos.lnk), the iCloud application directory, and all language resource folders (.lproj) were FileDeleted at 15:19:06–07 UTC. The sequential uninstall of the cloud-sync tool (iCloud) used for exfiltration and the track-cleaner (CCleaner) is consistent with a deliberate anti-forensics strategy to obscure exfiltration tooling.

top_findings.description: Eraser 6.2 secure-wipe pattern confirmed in USN Journal: $R Recycle Bin content files (including $RJEMT64.exe) received DataOverwrite|DataExtend|DataTruncation bursts at 15:13:38–15:13:49 UTC on 2015-03-25, immediately followed by FileDelete events at 15:14:44 UTC. The DataOverwrite+DataTruncation-then-Delete sequence is the characteristic signature of Eraser's DoD multi-pass overwrite. $RJEMT64.exe is an executable that was sent to Recycle Bin and then securely wiped — recovering its content is not forensically possible.
